short: A moderate German dance in four, often first in a suite
definition: A dance of German origin in a moderate four beats, usually the first dance of a Baroque suite, with a flowing line of quick notes.

short: The notes of a chord played one after another
definition: The notes of a chord played one after another instead of together.

short: Go straight on into the next movement, without a pause
definition: Italian for “attack”: the next movement begins at once, with no break, so the two are heard as one continuous piece.

short: A clarinet extended downwards, with extra low notes
definition: A clarinet with a longer body that reaches four semitones lower than the ordinary instrument. Mozart wrote his Clarinet Concerto for it.

short: Two keys sounding at the same time
definition: Music in two different keys at once, for example one hand of the piano in one key and the other hand in another. The clash gives a bright, slightly sour sparkle.

short: Two notes, then three, in the same span of time
definition: A rhythm typical of Anton Bruckner: two even notes followed by three notes squeezed into the same time (a triplet), often hammered out by the brass.

short: A free solo passage while the orchestra waits
definition: A short solo passage where the rest of the orchestra stops and one player or singer is free to linger.

short: One melody chasing itself, like a round
definition: One instrument plays a melody and another follows a moment later with the same melody, like a round.

short: Smooth and expressive, in a singing style
definition: “In a singing style”: played smoothly and expressively, like a voice.

short: Variations over a short, repeating pattern of chords
definition: A piece built on a short pattern of chords, often four or eight bars long, repeated again and again while the music above it keeps changing. Bach’s for solo violin is the best known.

short: Slow, hymn-like music in solemn chords
definition: Slow, hymn-like music that moves in solemn chords.

short: A scale that moves by every semitone, the smallest step
definition: A scale that climbs or falls through all twelve notes of the octave, each a semitone (the smallest step on the piano) from the next, so that it seems to slide rather than step.

short: The closing section that rounds off a movement
definition: A closing section added to the end of a movement.

short: Tapping the strings with the wood of the bow
definition: Tapping the strings with the wooden back of the bow, which makes a dry, clicking sound.

short: The bass line and chords that underpin Baroque music
definition: The accompaniment that runs under almost all Baroque music: a bass line played by a cello, bassoon or double bass, with a harpsichord, organ or lute filling in the chords.

short: Two or more independent melodies combined at once
definition: The art of combining two or more independent melodies so that they sound together as one texture, each keeping its own shape.

short: A lively “running” dance in three
definition: A “running” dance in three beats. The Italian corrente is quick and light; the French courante is more stately.

short: Getting gradually louder
definition: Getting gradually louder.

short: Themes that come back across a work’s movements
definition: A way of building a work in several movements so that themes from one movement return, often transformed, in the others.

short: The middle of sonata form, where the themes are worked
definition: The middle stage of sonata form, where the themes are broken up, combined and pushed through different keys.

short: A medieval chant for the dead, a symbol of death
definition: A medieval chant from the Mass for the dead. Composers quote it as a symbol of death.

short: A string section split to play separate lines
definition: A string section split into two or more groups, each playing a different line.

short: The themes presented twice: orchestra, then soloist
definition: In the first movement of a Classical concerto, the main themes are presented twice: first by the orchestra alone, then by the soloist with the orchestra, this time moving to a new key.

short: Two notes played at once on a string instrument
definition: Bowing two strings at the same time, so that a single violinist or cellist sounds two notes together.

short: A long-held low note, like a bagpipe’s
definition: One or more low notes held or repeated for a long time under a melody, like the drone pipes of a bagpipe.

short: Shostakovich’s musical signature: D, E-flat, C, B
definition: Shostakovich’s initials turned into notes. In German spelling, D. Sch. becomes D, Es (E-flat), C, H (B natural); he signed many works with this four-note motif.

short: A Slavic lament that swings between gloom and joy
definition: A Slavic word, from Ukrainian, for a brooding folk ballad. In Dvořák’s music it means a piece that switches suddenly between melancholy and high spirits.

short: The opening of sonata form, where the themes are introduced
definition: The first stage of sonata form, where the main themes are introduced. It is often repeated.

short: Two pianists sharing one keyboard
definition: Music for two pianists sitting side by side at one piano, one playing the upper part and the other the lower.

short: A slow, stately opening in jerky rhythms, then a fast section
definition: An opening piece in the style of the French court: a slow, grand section in jerky dotted rhythms, then a quick section in which the instruments enter one after another, often ending with a short return of the slow music.

short: A passage that begins like a fugue, then moves on
definition: A passage that starts like a fugue, with instruments entering one by one on the same tune, without being a full fugue.

short: One tune entering voice by voice, woven against itself
definition: A piece or section in which one tune enters in each voice in turn and is woven against itself.

short: A fast, fiery Czech folk dance in three beats
definition: A fast Bohemian folk dance for couples, usually in three beats, with accents that make the rhythm stumble into groups of two.

short: A stately old French dance in two, starting on the half-bar
definition: A French court dance of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, moderate in speed and in duple time, whose phrases begin in the middle of the bar. Composers kept writing gavottes long after people stopped dancing them.

short: A fast jig in skipping groups of three
definition: A fast dance descended from the British jig, in a skipping rhythm of three-note groups. It usually ends a Baroque suite.

short: A continuous slide from one note to another
definition: A continuous slide from one note to another.

short: A short bass line repeated under changing music
definition: A short bass line repeated over and over, while the music above it changes with each repeat.

short: High, glassy notes made by lightly touching a string
definition: High, glassy, almost flute-like notes, made on a string instrument by touching the string lightly at certain points instead of pressing it down.

short: Two bars of three beats regrouped into three pairs
definition: A rhythmic shift in which two bars of three beats are accented as if they were three groups of two, so they sound like one long bar of three slow beats. The beat seems to stumble or stretch.

short: Berlioz’s recurring melody that stands for a person
definition: “Fixed idea”: Berlioz’s term for a melody that represents a person and returns throughout a piece.

short: Music written to accompany a stage play
definition: Music composed for a production of a play: overtures, interludes between the acts, songs, dances and music under particular scenes.

short: A trumpet with holes and keys, able to play every note
definition: A trumpet of around 1800 with holes in its tube covered by keys, like a woodwind instrument, so that it could play a full chromatic scale. It was soon replaced by trumpets with valves.

short: A lively Polish dance from Kraków, with off-beat kicks
definition: A fast Polish folk dance from the Kraków region, in two beats, with syncopated accents that kick against the beat.

short: A lilting Polish country dance in three
definition: A folk dance from the Kujawy region of central Poland, in triple time like the mazurka but slower and more swaying.

short: A rustic Austrian dance in three, ancestor of the waltz
definition: A rustic Austrian country dance in three beats, a slower, heavier ancestor of the waltz.

short: A recurring theme tied to a character or idea
definition: A short theme linked to a character, object or idea, which returns whenever it appears or is meant. Wagner made the technique famous.

short: A German art song for voice and piano
definition: A German art song, usually a poem set for one voice with piano. Schubert wrote more than six hundred.

short: An old church scale: like a major scale with a raised fourth
definition: One of the old church modes. It sounds like a major scale with its fourth note raised a half step (F to F with B natural), which gives a bright, floating sound.

short: The kind of key that sounds bright or settled
definition: The kind of key that generally sounds bright or settled. Its darker counterpart is the minor.

short: A fast figure shooting up the notes of a chord
definition: A quick, bold melody that rises through the notes of a chord, named after the orchestra of Mannheim, which made it a trademark in the 18th century.

short: An elegant 18th-century dance in three beats
definition: An elegant 18th-century dance in three beats, used as the third movement of Classical symphonies.

short: A sacred choral piece on a Latin text
definition: A sacred piece for choir, usually unaccompanied, on a Latin text; one of the main forms of Renaissance church music.

short: A short musical idea that keeps returning
definition: The smallest musical idea, just a few notes, from which a theme is built.

short: Played with a device that softens and veils the sound
definition: Played with a small device on the instrument that softens and veils the sound.

short: Modern music that revives 18th-century forms and clarity
definition: A trend of the early twentieth century in which composers such as Prokofiev and Stravinsky borrowed the forms, textures and lightness of eighteenth-century music, while keeping modern harmonies and rhythms.

short: “Nobly”: a marking Elgar loved
definition: Italian for “nobly”. Elgar used the marking often, for broad, dignified melodies.

short: A dreamy “night piece”, usually for piano
definition: A “night piece”: a slow, dreamy piece with a singing melody over a flowing accompaniment, a form Chopin made famous.

short: An essential, prominent solo instrumental part
definition: A solo instrumental part that is essential and prominent throughout a movement.

short: Players placed out of sight, heard from a distance
definition: Instruments placed behind the stage or outside the hall, so that they sound far away.

short: A short pattern repeated over and over
definition: A short rhythm or melody repeated persistently, often underneath changing music.

short: A short theme repeated while the music around it changes
definition: A form in which a short theme repeats over and over while the music around it keeps changing.

short: One note held in the bass under changing harmony
definition: A single note held or repeated, usually in the bass, while the harmony changes above it.

short: A five-note scale heard in folk music worldwide
definition: A scale of five notes instead of the usual seven, with no semitone steps between them. It gives melodies an open, folk-like sound found in music all over the world.

short: Plucking the strings instead of using the bow
definition: Plucking the strings of a string instrument with the finger instead of using the bow.

short: Ancient unaccompanied church melody, in free rhythm
definition: The ancient melody of the Western Church, sung without accompaniment in a free, speech-like rhythm by one voice or many in unison. Also called plainsong or Gregorian chant.

short: Several independent melodies sounding together
definition: Music made of several independent melodic lines sung or played at once, each with its own shape, instead of one tune with accompaniment.

short: A small valveless horn once blown on mail coaches
definition: A small brass horn without valves, once blown by coachmen to announce the mail coach. It plays only a few notes, which gives it a simple, nostalgic sound.

short: Instrumental music that tells a story or paints a scene
definition: Instrumental music that tells a story or depicts a scene described by the composer.

short: The return of the opening themes near the end of sonata form
definition: The last stage of sonata form, where the opening themes return.

short: Music that follows the free rhythm of speech
definition: Music that imitates the rhythm of speech, free and unmeasured.

short: The returning refrain of a Baroque concerto
definition: In a Baroque concerto, the passage the whole ensemble plays at the start and brings back, often shortened or in new keys, between the soloist’s episodes.

short: A gentle, song-like piece or slow movement
definition: A tender, song-like piece; in the late 18th century often the title of a slow movement in a simple, lyrical style.

short: A main theme returning between contrasting episodes
definition: A form in which one main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

short: Stretching and pushing the tempo for expression
definition: “Robbed time”: the performer takes time in one place and gives it back in another, so that the tempo bends with the expression instead of staying strict.

short: A leaping Italian dance in quick triple time
definition: A fast, jumping folk dance from central Italy, especially around Rome; its name comes from the Italian *saltare*, “to jump”.

short: A slow, stately dance in three, stressing the second beat
definition: A slow, dignified dance in three beats, often with the weight on the second beat. It is the expressive centre of many Baroque suites.

short: A fast, energetic movement; the word means “joke”
definition: A fast, energetic movement, usually third in a symphony. The word means “joke”, though the mood is often far from funny.

short: Retuning a string instrument away from its normal tuning
definition: Tuning the strings of an instrument to different notes from the usual ones, for special chords or a different sound. In his Fourth Symphony Mahler asks for a solo violin tuned a whole tone higher.

short: A slow, swaying dance with a lilting long-short-long rhythm
definition: A slow, swaying piece in 6/8 or 12/8 with a lilting long-short-long rhythm, often used for gentle or melancholy music.

short: A symphony-like piece with several soloists
definition: A work for two or more solo instruments and orchestra, halfway between a symphony and a concerto; very fashionable in Paris in the 1770s.

short: Three stages: exposition, development, recapitulation
definition: A three-stage structure: themes are introduced (exposition), worked and set against each other (development), and brought back (recapitulation).

short: A small sonata form, often without a development
definition: A short, simple sonata form: the themes are presented and then return, with little or no development in between.

short: A set of dances in one key, played as one work
definition: A set of contrasting movements, usually dances, in the same key and played as one work. Bach also used the Italian word partita.

short: Bowing over the fingerboard for a soft, veiled tone
definition: Italian for “on the fingerboard”: the string player bows over the end of the fingerboard instead of near the bridge, which gives a soft, flute-like, veiled sound. French scores write *sur la touche*.

short: The piano pedal that keeps notes ringing after release
definition: The piano’s right-hand pedal. It lifts the dampers off the strings, so notes keep ringing after the keys are let go and blend into one another.

short: A one-movement orchestral piece that tells a story
definition: A single-movement orchestral work that describes a story, a place or a scene. The form was pioneered by Liszt.

short: Accents off the beat that pull against the pulse
definition: Accents placed off the main beats, which makes the rhythm feel as if it is floating or pulling against the pulse.

short: A whirling Italian dance in fast 6/8 time
definition: A fast, whirling folk dance from southern Italy in 6/8 time. Legend linked it to the bite of the tarantula spider.

short: One theme reshaped to take on a new character
definition: Changing a theme’s speed, rhythm, harmony or mood so that the same notes come back with a different character: a fierce idea, for example, reborn as a love song.

short: A rapid shimmer between two notes, or on one
definition: A rapid back-and-forth between two notes, or the fast repetition of one, which makes a shimmering or rumbling sound. On the piano it is often an octave in the left hand.

short: A rapid shake between two neighbouring notes
definition: A rapid alternation between a note and the note just above it, which makes the sound shimmer or, low on the piano, rumble.

short: The gentler middle section of a minuet or scherzo
definition: The contrasting middle section of a minuet or scherzo, usually gentler.

short: Wagner’s unresolved chord that opens *Tristan und Isolde*
definition: The first chord of Wagner’s *Tristan und Isolde*. It hangs in the air instead of resolving as the ear expects, and became a symbol of musical longing and of modern harmony.

short: The whole orchestra playing together
definition: Italian for “all”: the whole orchestra playing together, as opposed to the soloist.

short: Everyone playing the same notes at once
definition: Everyone playing the same notes at the same time.

short: A theme repeated with something changed
definition: A repeat of a theme in which something is changed: the decoration, the rhythm, the harmony or the instruments.

short: A horn-like brass instrument with a dark, soft tone
definition: A brass instrument made for Wagner’s Ring operas and played by horn players. Its tone is darker and rounder than a horn’s.

short: A dance in three beats, with a strong first beat
definition: A dance in three-four time that turns on a strong first beat followed by two lighter ones. It was the great ballroom dance of the nineteenth century.

short: A six-note scale of equal steps, with no home note
definition: A scale made only of whole steps, six notes to the octave. Because every step is the same size, no note sounds like home, which gives the music a floating, dreamlike quality. Debussy used it often.
